title: Maximum Subarray
statement: Given an integer array `nums`, return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray. The subarray must contain at least one element.
hints: Every pair of endpoints defines a subarray, and prefix sums turn each sum into a subtraction.
A negative running sum will never help a future element. Drop it.
Kadane keeps the best sum ending at i, which is max(nums[i], best_ending_here + nums[i]), and a separate global best.

approaches.name: All subarrays
approaches.explanation: Extend each start index until the end.

approaches.name: Kadane
approaches.explanation: Dynamic programming on the subarray that ends at the current index.

editorial: Let dp[i] be the maximum sum of a subarray that ends at i. Then dp[i] = nums[i] + max(dp[i-1], 0). The answer is the maximum dp[i]. Only the previous value is required, so two scalars replace the table. Initialize both from nums[0] so an all-negative array returns the largest element instead of zero.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def max_sub_array(nums: list[int]) -> int:
    best = running = nums[0]
    for value in nums[1:]:
        running = max(value, running + value)
        best = max(best, running)
    return best
